findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py lines 70-83, the new 'optimized_pagination' query parameter enables the OptimizedCursorPaginator only if the user is superuser or has global access. However, the check uses 'organization_context.member.has_global_access' without verifying if 'organization_context.member' is not None. If 'member' is None, this will raise an AttributeError, causing a 500 error for some requests.
findings.suggestion: Add a check to ensure 'organization_context.member' is not None before accessing 'has_global_access', e.g. 'enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or (organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)'.
findings.title: Potential AttributeError if organization_context.member is None

findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py lines 877-882, the code allows negative slicing offsets on Django querysets when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0. While Django ORM supports negative slicing, negative offsets can lead to unexpected behavior or inefficient queries depending on the database backend and queryset complexity. The comment claims this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level, but it does not address potential performance or correctness issues with negative offsets in slicing. This could cause subtle bugs or performance regressions when paginating backwards with negative offsets.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit tests for negative offset pagination to verify correctness and performance. Consider adding safeguards or alternative logic to handle negative offsets safely if issues arise.
findings.title: Negative offset slicing on queryset may cause performance or correctness issues

findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py lines 878-882, the code uses negative offsets directly on the queryset slice when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0. However, the slicing logic does not adjust for cursor.is_prev flag consistently in this branch, unlike the else branch where start_offset is adjusted based on cursor.is_prev. This inconsistency may cause incorrect slicing ranges or unexpected results when paginating backwards with negative offsets.
findings.suggestion: Ensure that slicing logic for negative offsets also considers cursor.is_prev flag consistently, similar to the else branch, to avoid incorrect slicing.
findings.title: Inconsistent slicing logic for negative offsets with cursor.is_prev flag

findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py lines 838-840 and 845-911, the OptimizedCursorPaginator overrides get_item_key and get_result but does not override or document the expected behavior of the 'key' attribute or how it interacts with the base class. If the base class expects 'key' to be set, it should be ensured that OptimizedCursorPaginator sets it properly. Lack of clarity here could cause unexpected behavior if 'key' is not set or used incorrectly.
findings.suggestion: Verify that 'key' attribute is properly initialized and documented in OptimizedCursorPaginator to avoid misuse.
findings.title: Potential unclear usage of 'key' attribute in OptimizedCursorPaginator

findings.body: In src/sentry/utils/cursors.py lines 26-28, the Cursor class constructor comment states that negative offsets are allowed for advanced pagination scenarios. However, there is no validation or enforcement of offset ranges. This could allow invalid negative offsets that might cause unexpected behavior downstream if not handled carefully in all paginator implementations.
findings.suggestion: Add validation or documentation clarifying valid offset ranges and expected behavior for negative offsets to prevent misuse.
findings.title: Cursor offset allows arbitrary negative values without validation

models.summary: The change introduces an OptimizedCursorPaginator with support for negative offsets and advanced pagination features, and integrates it into the organization audit logs endpoint for authorized users. The implementation generally follows existing patterns but has some risks around negative offset slicing on querysets and potential attribute errors due to missing null checks. The slicing logic for negative offsets is inconsistent regarding the cursor.is_prev flag, which may cause subtle bugs. Additional validation and testing are recommended to ensure robustness.
